"'''Bette Davis Eyes'''" is a song written and composed by [[Donna Weiss]] and [[Jackie DeShannon]] in 1974. It was recorded by DeShannon that year but made popular by [[Kim Carnes]] in 1981 when it spent nine non-consecutive weeks at the top of the U.S. [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]]. It won the 1982 [[Grammy Awards]] for [[Grammy Award for Song of the Year|Song of the Year]] and [[Record of the Year]].<ref name="All-Time">{{cite magazine|title= The Billboard Hot 100 All-Time Top Songs (20-11) |magazine= [[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]] |url= http://www.billboard.com/bbcom/specials/hot100/charts/top100-titles-20.shtml |archive-date= September 13, 2008 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20080913205950/http://www.billboard.com/bbcom/specials/hot100/charts/top100-titles-20.shtml}}</ref> The music video was directed by Australian film director [[Russell Mulcahy]].<ref>{{cite news|title= 80sonVEVO GAMV Takeover Week 9 w/ FEATURED VIDEO Kim Carnes' "Bette Davis Eyes" |date= March 20, 2013 |access-date= November 9, 2015 |url= http://goldenageofmusicvideo.com/80sonvevo-gamv-takeover-week-9-w-featured-video-kim-carnes-bette-davis-eyes}}</ref>

On the [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]], the song was No. 1 for five weeks, interrupted for just one week by "[[Stars on 45 (song)|Stars on 45]]" before it returned to the top spot for another four weeks, becoming [[Billboard (magazine)|''Billboard'']]{{'}}s biggest hit of the year.<ref name="Hot100"/> The single also reached No. 5 on ''Billboard''{{'}}s [[Mainstream Rock (chart)|Top Tracks charts]] and No. 26 on the Dance charts.<ref name="awards">{{cite web|title= Kim Carnes – Awards |publisher= [[AllMusic]] |access-date= May 3, 2014 |url= http://www.allmusic.com/artist/kim-carnes-mn0000097654/awards}}</ref> It reached No. 2 in Canada for twelve consecutive weeks, and was 1981's No. 2 hit in that country, after "Stars on 45".<ref name="Canada1"/><ref name="Canada2"/> It peaked at No. 10 in the [[United Kingdom]],<ref name="UK"/> to date Carnes's only Top 40 hit in that country. Additionally, it ranked No. 12 on ''Billboard''{{'}}s list of the top 100 songs in the first 50 years of the magazine's Hot 100.<ref name="All-Time" /> "Bette Davis Eyes" was a No. 1 hit in 21 countries.<ref name="#1"/>

"Bette Davis Eyes" is a song written and composed by Donna Weiss and Jackie DeShannon in 1974. It was recorded by DeShannon that year but made popular by Kim Carnes in 1981 when it spent nine non-consecutive weeks at the top of the U.S. Billboard Hot 100. It won the 1982 Grammy Awards for Song of the Year and Record of the Year. The music video was directed by Australian film director Russell Mulcahy.

On the Billboard Hot 100, the song was No. 1 for five weeks, interrupted for just one week by "Stars on 45" before it returned to the top spot for another four weeks, becoming Billboard{{'}}s biggest hit of the year. The single also reached No. 5 on Billboard{{'}}s Top Tracks charts and No. 26 on the Dance charts. It reached No. 2 in Canada for twelve consecutive weeks, and was 1981's No. 2 hit in that country, after "Stars on 45". It peaked at No. 10 in the United Kingdom, to date Carnes's only Top 40 hit in that country. Additionally, it ranked No. 12 on Billboard{{'}}s list of the top 100 songs in the first 50 years of the magazine's Hot 100. "Bette Davis Eyes" was a No. 1 hit in 21 countries.

sections.heading: Background
sections.wikitext:
[[File:Bette_Davis_-_Publicity_still_(1939).png|upright|thumb|left|[[Bette Davis]] in 1939]]
"Bette Davis Eyes" was written in 1974 by [[Donna Weiss]] and [[Jackie DeShannon]], the latter of whom recorded the song that same year for her album ''[[New Arrangement]]''.<ref>{{cite web|first= Saint |last= Cad |title= 10 More Famous Songs with Unknown Originals |website= Listverse |date= October 14, 2012 |access-date= June 21, 2013 |url= http://listverse.com/2012/10/14/10-more-famous-songs-with-unknown-originals/}}</ref> Weiss had traveled to DeShannon's house with a set of lyrics, including several additional verses that were ultimately scrapped. DeShannon refined some of the lyrics and also developed the song's music.<ref name="#1">{{cite book|first=Fred |last= Bronson |year= 1992 |title= Billboard Book of Number One Hits |edition= 3rd |publisher= Billboard Publications, Inc. |location= New York, NY |page= [https://archive.org/details/billboardbookofn0000bron/page/543 543] |isbn= 0-8230-8298-9 |url-access= registration |url= https://archive.org/details/billboardbookofn0000bron/page/543}}</ref> In this original incarnation, the track is performed in an "R&B lite" arrangement,<ref name="AM"/> featuring a prominent uptempo piano part, as well as flourishes of pedal steel guitar and horns.<ref>{{cite web|first= Mark |last= Deming |title= Jackie DeShannon – New Arrangement |publisher= AllMusic |access-date= June 10, 2014 |url= http://www.allmusic.com/album/new-arrangement-mw0000769197}}</ref> However, it was not until March 1981,<ref name="AUT"/> when Carnes recorded her version of the song in a radically different synthesizer-based arrangement, that it became a commercial success.

According to producer [[Val Garay]], the original demo of the tune that was brought to him sounded like "a [[Leon Russell]] track, with this beer-barrel polka piano part."{{efn|The demo can be heard in a TAXI TV interview with Garay, at 21:50.<ref>{{cite web|title= Legendary Producer Val Garay |publisher= [[IBM Cloud Video|Ustream]] |date= November 27, 2012 |access-date= May 3, 2014 |url= http://www.ustream.tv/recorded/27298334 |archive-date= November 5, 2013 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20131105144806/http://www.ustream.tv/recorded/27298334 |url-status= dead}}</ref>}} Carnes initially rejected the song based on the demo's arrangement, until keyboardist Bill Cuomo, using the [[Prophet-5]] synthesizer, came up with the signature riff that defines Carnes's version.<ref name="Mix">{{cite magazine|first= Blair |last= Jackson |title= Classic Tracks: Kim Carnes' "Bette Davis Eyes" |magazine= [[Mix (magazine)|Mix]] |url= http://mixonline.com/recording/interviews/audio_kim_carnes_bette/index.html |archive-date= July 13, 2014 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20140713100707/http://mixonline.com/recording/interviews/audio_kim_carnes_bette/index.html}}</ref> In an interview with [[Dick Clark]] on the ''National Music Survey'', Carnes credited Cuomo with the song's new arrangement, saying that "the minute he came up with that, then it fell into place. Everybody went, 'That's it!'"<ref name="#1"/>

Only three takes were recorded, the first of which was used with no [[overdubbing]]. Craig Krampf insisted on incorporating a [[Synare]] [[electronic drum]] into the song, although Garay objected to the instrument's inclusion on the grounds that it was "the most annoying thing I'd ever heard in my life." However, Garay changed his mind once Krampf hit the Synare on the chorus and found the instrument to be a great addition to the song. The drums were miked at close proximity using a [[Sennheiser MD 421]] on the bass drum, a [[Shure|Shure 56]] and [[Sennheiser MD 441]] on the snare drum, [[Telefunken|Telefunken 251s]] on the toms, and an [[AKG (company)|AKG 452]] on the hi-hat. Carnes sang her vocals through a [[Neumann U 47#Successors: U 48, U 67, U 87, and U 47 FET|Neumann U67]] microphone situated next to the [[mixing console]].<ref name="Mix"/>

Actress [[Bette Davis]] was 73 when Carnes's version became a hit. She wrote letters to Carnes, Weiss, and DeShannon to thank them for making her "a part of modern times" and said that her grandson now looked up to her. After their Grammy wins, Davis sent them roses and happily accepted the gift of gold and platinum records from Carnes, hanging them on her wall.<ref name="#1"/><ref>{{cite book|title=The Women of Warner Brothers: The Lives and Careers of 15 Leading Ladies, with Filmographies for Each |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=nmjetV92THsC&pg=PA49 |isbn=9780786411375 |last1=Bubbeo |first1=Daniel |date=October 29, 2001 |publisher=McFarland}}</ref>  The opening line, "Her hair is Harlow gold" is a tribute to starlet [[Jean Harlow]],<ref>{{cite news |title=Story of the song: Bette Davis Eyes by Kim Carnes |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/independentpremium/bette-davis-eyes-kim-carnes-b2220625.html |access-date=July 20, 2024 |work=[[The Independent]] |date=November 11, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221126020017/https://www.independent.co.uk/independentpremium/bette-davis-eyes-kim-carnes-b2220625.html |archive-date=November 26, 2022 |url-status=live}}</ref> the leading [[sex symbol]] of early 1930s films, often nicknamed the "Blonde Bombshell" and the "Platinum Blonde", whose look inspired Marilyn Monroe, Madonna, and others.<ref Who Inspired Marilyn Monroe | website=Vintage Everyday | date=2016-04-25 | url=https://www.vintag.es/2023/03/harlow-monroe-inspiration.html | access-date=2024-05-22}}</ref><ref name="k415">{{cite web sections.text:
upright|thumb|left|[[Bette Davis in 1939]]
"Bette Davis Eyes" was written in 1974 by Donna Weiss and Jackie DeShannon, the latter of whom recorded the song that same year for her album New Arrangement. Weiss had traveled to DeShannon's house with a set of lyrics, including several additional verses that were ultimately scrapped. DeShannon refined some of the lyrics and also developed the song's music. In this original incarnation, the track is performed in an "R&B lite" arrangement, featuring a prominent uptempo piano part, as well as flourishes of pedal steel guitar and horns. However, it was not until March 1981, when Carnes recorded her version of the song in a radically different synthesizer-based arrangement, that it became a commercial success.

According to producer Val Garay, the original demo of the tune that was brought to him sounded like "a Leon Russell track, with this beer-barrel polka piano part."{{efn|The demo can be heard in a TAXI TV interview with Garay, at 21:50.}} Carnes initially rejected the song based on the demo's arrangement, until keyboardist Bill Cuomo, using the Prophet-5 synthesizer, came up with the signature riff that defines Carnes's version. In an interview with Dick Clark on the National Music Survey, Carnes credited Cuomo with the song's new arrangement, saying that "the minute he came up with that, then it fell into place. Everybody went, 'That's it!'"

Only three takes were recorded, the first of which was used with no overdubbing. Craig Krampf insisted on incorporating a Synare electronic drum into the song, although Garay objected to the instrument's inclusion on the grounds that it was "the most annoying thing I'd ever heard in my life." However, Garay changed his mind once Krampf hit the Synare on the chorus and found the instrument to be a great addition to the song. The drums were miked at close proximity using a Sennheiser MD 421 on the bass drum, a Shure 56 and Sennheiser MD 441 on the snare drum, Telefunken 251s on the toms, and an AKG 452 on the hi-hat. Carnes sang her vocals through a Neumann U67 microphone situated next to the mixing console.

Actress Bette Davis was 73 when Carnes's version became a hit. She wrote letters to Carnes, Weiss, and DeShannon to thank them for making her "a part of modern times" and said that her grandson now looked up to her. After their Grammy wins, Davis sent them roses and happily accepted the gift of gold and platinum records from Carnes, hanging them on her wall.  The opening line, "Her hair is Harlow gold" is a tribute to starlet Jean Harlow, the leading sex symbol of early 1930s films, often nicknamed the "Blonde Bombshell" and the "Platinum Blonde", whose look inspired Marilyn Monroe, Madonna, and others.

sections.heading: Critical reception
sections.wikitext:
''[[Record World]]'' called it a "haunting pop-rocker" and said that Carnes's "earthy vocal rasp and guitar chimes are unforgettable."<ref name=rw>{{cite magazine|magazine=Record World|date=March 28, 1981|accessdate=February 19, 2023|title=Hits of the Week|page=1|url=https://worldradiohistory.com/Archive-All-Music/Record-World/80s/80/RW-1980-03-28.pdf}}</ref> Joe Viglione of [[AllMusic]] believed that "Bette Davis Eyes" was superior to all other tracks on ''Mistaken Identity''.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Viglione |first=Joe|title=Mistaken Identity - Kim Carnes |website=AllMusic |url=https://www.allmusic.com/album/mistaken-identity-mw0000837524 |access-date=November 1, 2024|language=en}}</ref>

sections.heading: Certifications
Gwyneth Paltrow version
sections.wikitext: American actress [[Gwyneth Paltrow]] covered "Bette Davis Eyes" for the soundtrack for the 2000 [[road trip]] film ''[[Duets (film)#Soundtrack|Duets]]''.<ref>{{cite web|first= Heather |last= Phares |title= Original Soundtrack – Duets [Original Soundtrack] |publisher= [[AllMusic]] |access-date= June 26, 2020 |url= https://www.allmusic.com/album/duets-original-soundtrack-mw0000098536}}</ref> This version was released as a single in Australia on March 26, 2001,<ref>{{cite web|title= New Releases Singles – Week Commencing 26th March 2001 |publisher= [[Australian Recording Industry Association|ARIA]] |page= 24 |date= March 26, 2001 |access-date= April 19, 2021 |url= http://www.aria.com.au/issue578.PDF |url-status= dead |archive-url= https://webarchive.nla.gov.au/awa/20020220130000/http://pandora.nla.gov.au/pan/23790/20020221-0000/www.aria.com.au/issue578.PDF |archive-date= February 20, 2002}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> debuting and peaking at No. 3 on the [[ARIA Charts|ARIA Singles Chart]] on April 8, 2001.<ref name="AUS">{{cite web|title= Australian-charts.com – Gwyneth Paltrow – Bette Davis Eyes |website= Australian-charts.com |access-date= June 26, 2020 |url= https://australian-charts.com/showitem.asp?interpret=Gwyneth+Paltrow&titel=Bette+Davis+Eyes&cat=s}}</ref> It spent nine weeks in the top 10,<ref name="AUS"/> and came in at No. 35 on Australia's year-end chart for 2001. It earned a platinum [[Music recording certification|certification]] from the [[Australian Recording Industry Association]] for shipping more than 70,000 units.<ref>{{cite web|title= 2001 ARIA Singles Chart |publisher= ARIA |access-date= June 26, 2020 |url= https://www.aria.com.au/charts/2001/singles-chart}}</ref>
sections.text: American actress Gwyneth Paltrow covered "Bette Davis Eyes" for the soundtrack for the 2000 road trip film Duets. This version was released as a single in Australia on March 26, 2001, debuting and peaking at No. 3 on the ARIA Singles Chart on April 8, 2001. It spent nine weeks in the top 10, and came in at No. 35 on Australia's year-end chart for 2001. It earned a platinum certification from the Australian Recording Industry Association for shipping more than 70,000 units.

sections.heading: Taylor Swift live performance
sections.wikitext: American singer [[Taylor Swift]] included a live performance cover of "Bette Davis Eyes" on her 2011 ''[[Speak Now World Tour – Live]]'' album.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Keefe |first=Jonathan |date=2011-11-28 |title=Review: Taylor Swift, Speak Now World Tour Live |url=https://www.slantmagazine.com/music/taylor-swift-speak-now-world-tour-live/ |access-date=2024-01-01 |website=Slant Magazine |language=en-US}}</ref>
sections.text: American singer Taylor Swift included a live performance cover of "Bette Davis Eyes" on her 2011 Speak Now World Tour – Live album.

sections.heading: Ethel Cain homage
sections.wikitext: American singer [[Ethel Cain]] performed the song at a concert in Paris as a tribute to [[old Hollywood]] in June 2024.<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Grow |first=Kory |date=2024-06-05 |title=See Ethel Cain Cover 'Bette Davis Eyes,' Debut Unreleased Songs in Paris |url=https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-news/ethel-cain-bette-davis-eyes-1235033588/ |access-date=2025-08-01 |magazine=Rolling Stone |language=en-US}}</ref> Cain released the single "[[Fuck Me Eyes]]," which has been interpreted as a spiritual "sequel" to the original, which she called one of her favorite songs ever.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Frank |first=Jason P. |date=2025-07-09 |title=A 44-Year Old Song Is the Queer Anthem of the Summer, for Better and Worse |url=https://www.vulture.com/article/jojo-siwa-ethel-cain-bette-davis-eyes.html |access-date=2025-08-01 |website=Vulture |language=en}}</ref>
sections.text: American singer Ethel Cain performed the song at a concert in Paris as a tribute to old Hollywood in June 2024. Cain released the single "Fuck Me Eyes," which has been interpreted as a spiritual "sequel" to the original, which she called one of her favorite songs ever.

sections.heading: JoJo Siwa cover
sections.wikitext: American reality star and singer [[JoJo Siwa]] released a version of the song on July 11, 2025.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=JoJo Siwa Releases Controversial 'Bette Davis Eyes' Cover — Original Singer Kim Carnes Might Not Be a Fan |url=https://people.com/jojo-siwa-releases-controversial-bette-davis-eyes-cover-11770479 |access-date=2025-08-01 |website=People.com |language=en}}</ref> She debuted the song at a live performance the previous May, dedicated to her boyfriend, reality star [[Chris Hughes (TV personality)|Chris Hughes]].<ref name=":0" /> Kim Carnes made a statement to [[TMZ]] criticizing the cover as "a bit too close" to her own version.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-07-17 |title="Bette Davis Eyes" Singer Kim Carnes Reveals Her True Thoughts on JoJo Siwa |url=https://www.eonline.com/news/1420004/bette-davis-eyes-singer-kim-carnes-on-jojo-siwa-cover |access-date=2025-08-01 |website=E! Online}}</ref>
sections.text: American reality star and singer JoJo Siwa released a version of the song on July 11, 2025. She debuted the song at a live performance the previous May, dedicated to her boyfriend, reality star Chris Hughes. Kim Carnes made a statement to TMZ criticizing the cover as "a bit too close" to her own version.

sections.heading: In popular media
sections.wikitext: Kim Carnes' version of the song has appeared in various films and TV series including ''[[200 Cigarettes]]'' (1999), ''[[Cold Case]]'' S1E6 (2003), ''[[That's My Boy (2012 film)|That's My Boy]]'' (2012) ''[[The Final Girls]]'' (2015), ''[[American Horror Story]]'' [[American Horror Story: Hotel|S5]]E5 (2015), [[Riverdale (American TV series)|''Riverdale'']] [[Riverdale season 2|S2]]E18 (2018), ''[[The After Party (film)|The After Party]]'' (2018), ''[[Anaïs in Love]]'' (2021), ''[[The Tourist (TV series)|The Tourist]]'' S1E1 (2022), ''[[Angelyne (miniseries)|Angelyne]]'' S1E3 (2022), ''[[MaXXXine]]'' (2024) and ''[[And Just Like That...]]'' S3 E7.{{citation needed|date=August 2025}}
